what_happened: The operator wrote a correction to job 20261024-154552-e65v. It required a test fixture and a doc comment to name the operator/ directory. The boundary test in xtask/tests/policy.rs bans that word in Athena's files. The producer used owner-notes/ instead, which was the right call. The verifier then judged the criterion unmet, because the criterion itself asked for banned text. The operator's own correction caused the failure.
cause: The author of a request, correction or criterion is not shown the boundary test's banned-word list. Nothing scans the wording of corrections or criteria against that list before the job runs. A requirement to write a banned word can therefore be accepted, and the conflict only appears when the producer departs from it and the verifier judges the result. The same cause produced an earlier mistake on 2026-10-17, so it is a standing gap and not a one-off slip.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance and at correction intake. It takes the banned-word list that xtask/tests/policy.rs uses, scans every literal text, name or path that a criterion or correction requires to appear in Athena's files, and rejects the reading or correction with the offending word named. The list should come from one shared source, so the scan and the boundary test cannot drift apart. The same list should also be shown to the operator and the reader when they write requests. This covers the whole class, whether the banned word is written by the producer or demanded by a criterion.
proposed_request: Make Athena check requests, corrections and acceptance criteria against the boundary scan's banned-word list before any job runs. Outcome: if a correction or criterion requires text, a name or a path in Athena's files that contains a word the boundary test in xtask/tests/policy.rs bans, Athena refuses it at intake. The refusal names the word and suggests that the author use a neutral term. The scan and the boundary test must read the same single word list. Show that list to the reader and to the correction intake step. Tests: (1) a criterion that requires the directory name operator/ is refused; (2) a criterion that uses owner-notes/ is accepted; (3) changing the shared list changes both the intake check and the boundary test.
